rules: Set a project up once: `npx hlmnhkl-ui@latest init` (copies tokens.css and base.css, writes hlmnhkl-ui.json).
Add components: `npx hlmnhkl-ui@latest add <name>`. Their imports come along. See all names: `npx hlmnhkl-ui list`.
Style with the `--hl-*` tokens, never raw colours or sizes. Theme by changing tokens, not component CSS.
Every component is accessible by default: keep the labels, roles and keyboard behaviour it ships with.
Items marked Pro are not in the free package and cannot be installed with the CLI.

items.name: Button
items.description: A pill button with four variants, a soft edge that dents where you press, leans toward a nearby mouse and sends one small wave round when let go, and a loading state that morphs the label into a spinner.
a11y: Real <button>, so Enter and Space work.
Loading sets aria-busy and ignores clicks, but keeps focus in place.
aria-disabled looks like disabled but stays focusable and ignores clicks, so focus is not lost and the linked reason can still be read.
With href it renders a real <a>, for navigation. Disabled, the link drops its href.
Small size keeps a 44px hit area with an invisible layer.
Danger is solid red with a bolder label. The label names the action, so it never relies on colour alone.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant? | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost' \| 'danger'` | `'primary'` | Visual weight. Use one primary per view and danger for destructive actions. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Height and text size. |
| loading? | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a spinner and ignores clicks, but keeps focus on the button. |
| loadingLabel? | `string` | `'Loading'` | Spoken while loading, for example "Saving". |
| leadingIcon? | `ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label. |
| trailingIcon? | `ReactNode` |  | Icon after the label. |
| fullWidth? | `boolean` |  | Stretches the button to fill its container. |
| href? | `string` |  | Renders a link with the same look, for navigation. Button-only props such as type are then ignored. |

items.example:
const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)

<Button loading={saving} loadingLabel="Saving" onClick={save}>
  Save changes
</Button>

items.name: IconButton
items.description: A round button for a single icon. The label prop is required and becomes the accessible name.
a11y: label is required and set as aria-label.
Visual size can be 32px; the hit area is always 44px.
Pair with Tooltip so mouse users can read the label too.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Required: the accessible name, since the button has no visible text. |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | The icon to show. It is the only visible content. |
| variant? | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'ghost'` | `'ghost'` | Visual weight. Ghost has no fill until hover. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Size of the button. |

items.example:
<Tooltip content="Edit">
  <IconButton label="Edit" icon={<EditIcon />} />
</Tooltip>
<IconButton label="Settings" variant="secondary" icon={<SettingsIcon />} />
<IconButton label="Add item" variant="primary" icon={<PlusIcon />} />

items.name: Fab
items.description: One main action floating in the thumb zone. Extended, its label pours away into the icon as the page scrolls down. With actions, a tap pours a short stack of them up out of the button.
a11y: A real <button>. Round, its label is the aria-label; extended, the label is the visible text.
With actions it has aria-expanded and aria-controls. Opening moves focus to the first action; Esc or a tap outside closes them and returns focus to the button.
Closed actions are inert, so Tab never lands on a hidden one.
56px round, and each action keeps a 44px hit area.
It sits above the home indicator (env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). With reduced motion the label and actions switch at once.
Use one per screen, for the one action people come for. Everything else belongs in the page.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | The button's name. Shown as text when extended, and always read by screen readers. |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | The icon in the button, such as a plus. With actions it turns a quarter while they are open. |
| onClick? | `() => void` |  | Called on tap. With actions, a tap opens them instead. |
| extended? | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the label beside the icon. It pours away into the icon as the page scrolls down, and back on the way up. |
| actions? | `FabAction[]` |  | A short stack of actions that pours up out of the button when it is tapped. |
| position? | `'end' \| 'center'` | `'end'` | Where it sits along the bottom of the screen. |
| contained? | `boolean` | `false` | Sits at the bottom of its nearest positioned parent instead of the screen, for a demo or a panel. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<Fab
  label="New job"
  icon={<PlusIcon />}
  actions={[
    { label: 'Start a job', icon: <EditIcon />, onSelect: startJob },
    { label: 'Share the day', icon: <ShareIcon />, onSelect: share },
    { label: 'Export', icon: <DownloadIcon />, onSelect: exportDay },
  ]}
/>

items.name: ThemeToggle
items.description: One button that flips between the light and dark theme: the sun turns into the moon and back. On its own it sets data-theme on the page and remembers the choice; themeScript stops a saved dark theme flashing light on load.
a11y: Its name says what it does next, "Switch to dark theme", so the icon alone never has to explain it.
With no saved choice the page follows the system setting.
If storage is blocked the theme still changes for the visit; nothing breaks.
The icon turn uses motion tokens, so reduced motion switches it at once.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| theme? | `'light' \| 'dark'` |  | The theme, when your app keeps it. Leave it out and the toggle sets data-theme on <html> itself. |
| onThemeChange? | `(theme: Theme) => void` |  | Called with the new theme on every flip. |
| storageKey? | `string` | `'hl-theme'` | Where the choice is remembered when the toggle runs the page. Match it in themeScript. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'sm'` | The button's size, the same as IconButton. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the button. |

items.name: Toggle
items.description: One button that stays pressed until it is pressed again. The fill pops in, so the state reads at a glance.
a11y: A real <button> with aria-pressed, so Enter and Space switch it and screen readers say pressed or not pressed.
Keep the label the same in both states; aria-pressed already says which one it is.
Icon only: pass aria-label, since there is no visible text to name it.
Pressed is a solid fill, not a faint shade, so it does not rely on colour alone.
The small size keeps a 44px hit area with an invisible layer.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pressed? | `boolean` |  | Pressed state, when you control it. |
| defaultPressed? | `boolean` | `false` | Starting pressed state when you do not control it. |
| onPressedChange? | `(pressed: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the button is pressed or let go, with the new state. |
| icon? | `ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label. Without a label the button is round and needs an aria-label. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Height and text size, the same as Button. |

items.example:
const [unread, setUnread] = useState(false)

<Toggle size="sm" pressed={unread} onPressedChange={setUnread}>Unread only</Toggle>
<Toggle icon={<BellIcon />}>Notify me</Toggle>
<Toggle size="lg">Show archived</Toggle>

items.name: ButtonGroup
items.description: Joins related buttons into one bar. Neighbours share a border, and only the ends are rounded.
a11y: role="group" with the label you give, so screen readers say what the buttons are for.
Each button stays its own Tab stop with its own name.
The focused button rises above its neighbours, so its whole focus ring shows.
For one choice out of several, use SegmentedControl or ToggleGroup instead: they say which one is picked.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Accessible name for the group, such as "Text alignment". |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The Button, IconButton or Toggle elements to join. Secondary ones show the shared borders best. |
| orientation? | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | A row, or a column where each button takes the full width. |

items.example:
<ButtonGroup label="File actions">
  <Button variant="secondary" leadingIcon={<DownloadIcon />}>Download</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary" leadingIcon={<ShareIcon />}>Share</Button>
  <IconButton variant="secondary" label="More file actions" icon={<ChevronDownIcon />} />
</ButtonGroup>

items.name: Link
items.description: A text link with a quiet resting underline and a solid one that sweeps in on hover.
a11y: Always underlined, so it never relies on colour.
external adds rel="noopener noreferrer" and says "opens in a new tab".

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| external? | `boolean` |  | Opens in a new tab, adds a safe rel and an arrow, and tells screen readers. |
| variant? | `'inline' \| 'standalone'` | `'inline'` | Inline sits in running text. Standalone gets a full-size touch target. |
| labels? | `Partial<LinkLabels>` |  | Screen reader text, so you can translate it. Missing keys use the English defaults. |

items.example:
<Link href="/tokens">design tokens</Link>
<Link variant="standalone" href="/buttons">View all buttons</Link>
<Link external href="https://developer.mozilla.org/">MDN docs</Link>

items.name: CopyButton
items.description: Copies text to the clipboard. A drop falls from where you press into the icon and fills it, the icon becomes a check, and then it turns back.
a11y: Announces "Copied" through a polite live region.
Falls back to execCommand when the Clipboard API is blocked.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `string` |  | Text to put on the clipboard. |
| label? | `string` | `'Copy'` | Accessible name, and the visible text when showLabel is on. |
| copiedLabel? | `string` | `'Copied'` | Shown and spoken after a successful copy. |
| failedLabel? | `string` | `'Could not copy'` | Shown and spoken when the browser blocks the copy. |
| showLabel? | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the label as text next to the icon. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Size of the button. |
| resetAfter? | `number` | `1800` | How long the check or the failed state stays, in ms. |
| onCopy? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called after the text is copied, with the copied text. Not called if copying fails. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the button. |

items.example:
<CopyButton value="npm run dev" />
<CopyButton value={inviteUrl} label="Copy link" copiedLabel="Link copied" showLabel />

items.name: SwipeActions
items.description: Swipe a row sideways to show its actions, as in a mail app. Let go and the row carries on at the speed of your swipe: past half way or on a flick it stays open, and a full swipe throws it off and runs the outer action.

items.name: HoldToConfirm
items.description: Press and hold to run a risky action. A line burns along the button's own edge, out both ways from your finger, and the action runs when the ends meet. Let go early and it runs back. One tap or key press opens a Cancel and Confirm step in place instead.
a11y: One press of Enter or Space, a screen reader or voice control opens the confirm step, since holding a key is hard for many people. Focus moves to Cancel.
Escape closes the step and gives focus back to the button.
Nothing runs on press: letting go early cancels, so it passes WCAG 2.5.2.
The hint under the button is its description. The result is read by a polite live region.
With reduced motion the line still fills, since it is a timer, and the step opens with no glide.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The action, as the button's label, such as "Delete workspace". |
| onConfirm | `() => void` |  | Called once the hold runs to the end, or Confirm is pressed in the confirm step. |
| onCancel? | `() => void` |  | Called when a hold is let go early, or the confirm step is cancelled. |
| confirmLabel? | `string` | `'Confirm'` | The confirm step's button, such as "Delete". Keep it short. |
| cancelLabel? | `string` | `'Cancel'` | The confirm step's way back. |
| doneLabel? | `ReactNode` | `'Done'` | Shown in place of the label once it is done, such as "Workspace deleted". |
| hint? | `ReactNode` | `'Hold to confirm, or tap for a confirm step.'` | The line under the button. Defaults to how to use it. |
| stepHint? | `ReactNode` |  | The line under the button while the confirm step is open. |
| disabled? | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks the button. Say why in the hint. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the outer box. |

items.example:
<HoldToConfirm onConfirm={reset} confirmLabel="Reset" doneLabel="Speaker reset" hint="Hold to reset, or tap for a confirm step.">
  Reset speaker
</HoldToConfirm>

items.name: MorphButton
items.description: A button that grows into its own panel from where it sits. The label stays on the same spot and becomes the panel's title, and nothing on the page moves. It folds back into the button when it closes.
a11y: The button has aria-expanded and aria-haspopup="dialog". The panel is a dialog named by the label.
Opening moves focus to the first control in the panel. Escape, the close button or a tap outside closes it and gives focus back to the button.
Tab past the end of the panel closes it, since the page behind stays usable.
It grows toward the side with room and never runs past the edge of the screen.
With reduced motion it opens and closes at once.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | The button's text. It stays on the same spot and becomes the panel's title and name. |
| icon? | `ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | What the panel holds, such as a short form or a list of choices. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel is open, when you control it. |
| defaultOpen? | `boolean` | `false` | Starting open state when you do not control it. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new open state. |
| width? | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'sm'` | How wide the panel grows. It never runs past the edge of the screen. |
| closeLabel? | `string` | `'Close'` | Screen reader name for the close button. |
| initialFocus? | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | Element to focus when it opens. Defaults to the first control in the panel. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the outer box, which keeps the button's place in the page. |

items.example:
<MorphButton label="Share" icon={<ShareIcon />}>
  <Input label="Link" readOnly value={link} />
  <RadioGroup label="Who can open it" value={who} onValueChange={setWho}>
    <Radio value="link" label="Anyone with the link" />
    <Radio value="invite" label="Only people I invite" />
  </RadioGroup>
</MorphButton>

items.name: SwipeDeck
items.description: A stack of cards: throw the top one to either side to decide. A small ruler under the card has two throw marks, the next card rises as you pull, and the button for that side fills toward it. Undo plays the throw in reverse.
a11y: The deck is a group in the tab order, named by label. Arrow Left and Arrow Right throw the top card to that side, and Backspace brings the last one back.
Two buttons with words do the same as a throw, and a third button undoes. Each is at least 44px.
One polite status says each decision once, with the next card and the count, such as "Saved: Two rooms above a bakery. Card 2 of 6".
The cards behind the top one are inert and hidden from screen readers.
A card is thrown past 35% of its width, or by a flick over 600 px a second that moved at least 40px. A slow, short drag comes back. Up and down still scroll the page.
With reduced motion a decided card fades out, and undo fades it back in.
In a right-to-left page the start side is on the right; onDecide always says start or end.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `T[]` |  | The cards, top card first. The top card is the first whose key is not decided yet, so you may remove decided ones. |
| getKey | `(item: T) => string` |  | A key that stays the same for each item. |
| getName | `(item: T) => string` |  | A short name for an item, said by screen readers after each decision. |
| renderCard | `(item: T) => ReactNode` |  | Draws one card. |
| label | `string` |  | Screen reader name of the deck, such as "Flats to rent". |
| actions? | `[string, string]` | `['Pass', 'Save']` | The two button words, for the start side then the end side. |
| decided? | `[string, string]` | `['Passed', 'Saved']` | What screen readers say was done, start then end, such as "Passed" and "Saved". |
| onDecide? | `(item: T, side: SwipeDeckSide) => void` |  | Called once for each card, when it has been thrown or a button or key decided it. |
| onUndo? | `(item: T) => void` |  | Called when Undo brings a card back. If you removed it from items, put it back here. |
| undoLabel? | `string` | `'Undo the last decision'` | Screen reader name of the undo button. |
| empty? | `ReactNode` | `'That was the last card.'` | Shown when every card has been decided. |

items.example:
<SwipeDeck
  items={flats}
  getKey={(f) => f.id}
  getName={(f) => f.title}
  renderCard={(f) => <FlatCard flat={f} />}
  label="Flats to rent"
  actions={['Pass', 'Save']}
  decided={['Passed', 'Saved']}
  onDecide={(flat, side) => side === 'end' && save(flat)}
/>

items.name: Sparkline
items.description: A tiny line or area with no axes. It draws in from the left and morphs to new data. A dot marks the latest value.

items.name: Chart
items.description: Bar (grouped, stacked or across), line, area, donut, scatter, funnel, bullet and heatmap charts for dashboards. They draw in on mount, morph to new data, and redraw at any width. Series take a survey map's colours in a fixed order, and differ by dash, marker and texture too.

items.name: CalendarHeatmap
items.description: Activity by day as a grid of small squares: weeks as columns, weekdays as rows. Darker means more. It opens on the latest week and scrolls sideways on a small screen.

items.name: ChatThread
items.description: A chat: bubbles grouped by sender and time, day separators, delivery state with retry, and a message box where Enter sends.

items.name: CommentThread
items.description: Comments with replies two levels deep, reply and edit in place, relative times, and long threads folded behind "Show more".

items.name: NotificationInbox
items.description: Notifications with unread state, mark one or all as read, All and Unread tabs and a calm empty state. NotificationBell opens it from a Popover.

items.name: Badge
items.description: A small status label. New values pop in; a pulsing dot marks something live.
a11y: Plain text, read in place.
The pulse turns off with reduced motion.
Tones add colour only for a real status. The word in the badge still says it, so colour is never alone.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant? | `'solid' \| 'outline' \| 'subtle'` | `'subtle'` | Visual weight: filled, outlined or a soft tint. |
| tone? | `'neutral' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `'neutral'` | Status colour. Use it only for a real status, and keep a word in the badge. |
| dot? | `boolean \| 'pulse'` |  | A small dot before the text. "pulse" makes it breathe, for live states. |

items.example:
<Badge variant="solid">Solid</Badge>
<Badge variant="outline" dot>Draft</Badge>
<Badge dot="pulse">Live</Badge>
<Badge variant="solid">{count} new</Badge>

items.name: Tag
items.description: Removable tags fold their width away so neighbours slide in. Selectable chips grow a check.
a11y: Remove button is named "Remove <text>".
Selectable chips are buttons with aria-pressed.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Text of the tag. Plain text also names the remove button. |
| onRemove? | `() => void` |  | Shows a remove button. Called after the exit animation ends. |
| removeLabel? | `string` |  | Label for the remove button. Wins over labels.remove, which defaults to "Remove <text>". |
| selected? | `boolean` |  | Makes the tag a toggle chip (aria-pressed). |
| onSelectedChange? | `(selected: boolean) => void` |  | Called when a toggle chip is pressed, with the new selected state. |
| icon? | `ReactNode` |  | Icon before the text. Not shown on toggle chips, which show a check. |
| labels? | `Partial<TagLabels>` |  | Screen reader text, so you can translate it. Missing keys use the English defaults. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<Tag onRemove={() => remove('Design')}>Design</Tag>
<Tag selected={on} onSelectedChange={setOn}>Assigned to me</Tag>

items.name: Avatar
items.description: A photo that sharpens in over initials. AvatarGroup stacks them.
a11y: role="img" named by the person, plus status.
Status reads by fill (solid, half, hollow), not colour.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` |  | Used for the alt text and the initials fallback. |
| src? | `string` |  | Image URL. Initials show while it loads and if it fails. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` | Diameter of the avatar. |
| status? | `'online' \| 'away' \| 'offline'` |  | Shows a status dot and adds the status to the spoken name. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<Avatar name="Web engineer" src={url} status="online" />
<Avatar name="Design lead" size="lg" />

<AvatarGroup max={4} label="Project members">
  <Avatar name="Product lead" src={a} />
  …
</AvatarGroup>

items.name: AvatarGroup
items.description: Avatars stacked with an overlap, then a "+N" for the rest. The stack fans out on hover.
a11y: role="group", named with the label and every person in it, the hidden ones too.
The "+N" counter is named "N more", and its tooltip lists who they are.
Each avatar keeps its own name, plus status when it has one.
Hover is only a flourish: everyone is named without it.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The Avatar elements to stack, in order. |
| max? | `number` | `4` | Avatars shown before the "+N" counter. |
| size? | `AvatarProps['size']` | `'md'` | Size of the "+N" counter. Set it to match the avatars inside. |
| label? | `string` |  | What the people are, such as "Project members". Screen readers hear it with every name. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<AvatarGroup max={4} label="Reviewers">
  <Avatar name="Team lead" src={teamLead} />
  <Avatar name="Design lead" src={designLead} />
  <Avatar name="Web engineer" />
  <Avatar name="QA lead" src={qaLead} />
  <Avatar name="Support lead" />
  <Avatar name="Writer" />
  <Avatar name="Data analyst" />
</AvatarGroup>

items.name: Card
items.description: A soft panel with a large radius. Interactive cards lift on hover and zoom their media a touch.
a11y: Put a real link or button inside; the card shows its focus ring.
Title is an h3 by default.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title? | `ReactNode` |  | Heading at the top of the body, rendered as an h3. Any content, not the native tooltip. |
| description? | `ReactNode` |  | Muted text under the title. |
| media? | `ReactNode` |  | Media or a header slot shown above the body, edge to edge. |
| footer? | `ReactNode` |  | Row under the body, set apart by a border, such as actions. |
| interactive? | `boolean` |  | Lifts on hover. Use when the card holds a link or button that covers it. |
| padding? | `'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Space inside the card. |
| fill? | `boolean` |  | Lets the body grow when the card is stretched (a grid cell or flex row), so the footer or a last button sits at the bottom. |

items.example: } title="Version 3.0 launch" footer={} />

items.name: Kbd
items.description: A keycap. With listen, it presses down while you hold the real key.
a11y: Native <kbd> element.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The key name to show, such as "Esc" or "⌘". |
| listen? | `string` |  | A KeyboardEvent.key value. When set, the key presses down while the real key is held. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the kbd element. |

items.example: <Kbd listen="Meta">⌘</Kbd> <Kbd listen="k">K</Kbd>

items.name: CodeBlock
items.description: Code with light colouring for TSX, HTML, CSS and shell, a title row and a copy button. Line numbers on request.
a11y: The code is a <pre> that Tab reaches, named by the title, so long lines scroll with the arrow keys.
Line numbers are hidden from screen readers and left out when the code is selected or copied.
The copy button says "Copied" through a polite live region.
Colour only adds to the text: keywords and tags are also bold and comments are italic.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| code | `string` |  | The code to show and copy. |
| language? | `'tsx' \| 'html' \| 'css' \| 'shell'` |  | Sets the colouring. Undefined guesses from the first line. |
| title? | `string` |  | File name or short title in the header row. Undefined shows the language. |
| header? | `ReactNode` |  | Replaces the title in the header row, for example with tabs that switch the code. |
| lineNumbers? | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a line number before each line. They are never copied or read out. |
| copyable? | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the copy button in the header row. |
| copyLabel? | `string` | `'Copy code'` | Screen reader name for the copy button. |
| label? | `string` |  | Screen reader name for the scrollable code. Undefined uses the title. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example: <CodeBlock title="useOnline.ts" lineNumbers code={source} />

items.name: Divider
items.description: A 1px line. It draws in from the centre once, then stays still.
a11y: role="separator" with aria-orientation.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| orientation? | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | Direction of the line. A vertical line stretches to the height of its flex row. |
| label? | `ReactNode` |  | Text in the middle of a horizontal line, such as "or". |
| animated? | `boolean` | `true` | Draws the line in from the centre when it mounts. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<Divider />
<Divider label="or" />
<Divider orientation="vertical" />

items.name: AnimatedNumber
items.description: Each digit rolls to its new value on a 0 to 9 strip. Any Intl.NumberFormat style works.
a11y: Screen readers get the plain formatted value; the rolling digits are hidden.
Wrap in aria-live if changes must be announced.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `number` |  | Number to show. Digits roll to the new value when it changes. |
| format? | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions` |  | Passed to Intl.NumberFormat, for currency, percent, decimals and so on. |
| locale? | `string` |  | Locale for number formatting. Undefined uses the browser locale. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<AnimatedNumber value={count} />
<AnimatedNumber value={49} format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'MYR' }} locale="en-MY" />

items.name: Table
items.description: Data in rows with sortable columns, groups, a sticky header and optional selection. Rows glide to their new place after a sort, and snap into their group when it changes. On a narrow screen it scrolls sideways with the first column in place; layout="stack" turns rows into cards instead.
a11y: A real table with a caption. Sortable headers are buttons, and the header cell carries aria-sort.
Presses go ascending, descending, then back to unsorted. Each one is announced in a status region, such as "Sorted by Name, ascending".
Each row checkbox is named after the row; the header checkbox shows a mixed state.
Each group is its own row group with a row header, so screen readers announce the group as you move into it.
Explicit table roles keep the semantics when rows restyle as cards (layout="stack", under 560px of width).

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| columns | `TableColumn<T>[]` |  | The columns, in order, and how each one reads and shows a row. |
| rows | `T[]` |  | The data, one item per row. |
| getRowId | `(row: T) => string` |  | Returns a stable, unique id for a row. Used for keys, selection and sort motion. |
| caption | `string` |  | Always required. Names the table for screen readers. |
| hideCaption? | `boolean` |  | Hides the caption visually but keeps it for screen readers. |
| sort? | `TableSort \| null` |  | Current sort column and direction, when you control it. Null means unsorted. |
| defaultSort? | `TableSort \| null` | `null` | Starting sort when you do not control it. |
| onSortChange? | `(sort: TableSort \| null) => void` |  | Called with the new sort when a header is pressed: ascending, descending, then null. |
| groupBy? | `(row: T) => string` |  | Gathers rows under a header per group, such as each row's status. Groups keep the order they first appear in; the sort applies inside each group. Rows glide to their group when it changes. |
| selectable? | `boolean` |  | Adds a checkbox column. |
| selected? | `string[]` |  | Ids of the selected rows, when you control it. |
| defaultSelected? | `string[]` | `[]` | Starting selection when you do not control it. |
| onSelectedChange? | `(ids: string[]) => void` |  | Called when the selection changes, with the new list of row ids. |
| rowLabel? | `(row: T) => string` |  | Names each row checkbox, such as the person's name. Defaults to the first column's value. |
| layout? | `'scroll' \| 'stack'` | `'scroll'` | On a narrow screen: 'scroll' keeps the table and scrolls it sideways with the first column in place; 'stack' turns each row into a card with its labels. |
| maxHeight? | `CSSProperties['maxHeight']` |  | Scrolls the body under a sticky header past this height. |
| emptyText? | `ReactNode` | `'Nothing here yet.'` | Shown in place of rows when there are none. |
| labels? | `Partial<TableLabels>` |  | Screen reader text for checkboxes and sort news. Missing keys use the English defaults. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.name: Timeline
items.description: Steps in order. They rise in one by one when the list scrolls into view, and each line draws down to the next.

items.name: Stat
items.description: A KPI card: label, a value whose digits roll, and the change with an arrow that turns. Pair it with a Sparkline.

items.name: TreeView
items.description: Nested folders that open with a smooth height change. The selected row fills in, and the chevron turns. With onMove, items can be dragged into folders, or moved with the keyboard.

items.name: KanbanBoard
items.description: Columns of cards you can drag between and within columns. The card lifts and tilts, others glide out of its way, and it settles into place on drop. On a phone, hold a card for a moment, then drag.

items.name: DescriptionList
items.description: Label and value pairs, such as billing details. Side by side or stacked, with an optional copy button per value.

items.name: RelativeTime
items.description: Shows a moment as "5 minutes ago" or "in 3 days" in any locale, keeps it fresh, and gives the full date on hover.

items.name: Countdown
items.description: Counts down to a date or for a set time with rolling digits. Pauses, and tells you when it ends.

items.name: SplitFlap
items.description: Letters and numbers that flip into place like a station board. Each cell runs forward through its drum, fast and then slower, and lands with no bounce. When the text gets longer or shorter, the board grows or shrinks with the liquid morph.
a11y: The text is in the page once, in a hidden node. The flipping cells are hidden from screen readers.
The new text is said once, politely, when every cell has landed. Turn announce off when one message covers a whole board.
A change in the middle of a run goes straight on to the newest text.
A cell passes 8 letters at most and the cells start within 350ms of each other, so a change ends inside a second.
With reduced motion the new text shows at once.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `string` |  | The text the board shows. A change flips each cell forward through the drum to its new letter. |
| length? | `number` | `0` | At least this many cells: shorter text is padded with blank ones, so a column keeps its width. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Text size of the cells. |
| chars? | `string` | `SPLIT_FLAP_CHARS` | The drum's letters, in the order a cell passes them. A letter that is not on it flips straight in. |
| announce? | `boolean` | `true` | Says the new text to screen readers once, when the board has landed. Turn off when one message covers several boards. |
| onSettle? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called once with the text when every cell has landed. |

items.example: <SplitFlap value={sailing.status} size="sm" announce={false} onSettle={(v) => landed(sailing.time, v)} />

items.name: SortableList
items.description: A list you put in order by dragging its handles. The other rows slide aside, the dragged row is drawn into the gap where it will land, and it settles there when dropped.

items.name: VirtualList
items.description: A long list that draws only the rows in view, so ten thousand rows scroll as fast as ten. Rows can be one fixed height or measured as they draw.

items.name: DataGrid
items.description: A spreadsheet-like grid for big data sets. Ten thousand rows scroll smoothly, since only the rows in view are drawn. Sort by one or more columns, resize and pin them, filter from each header, search all of it and select rows.

items.name: Calendar
items.description: A month grid for one date, a range or many dates. Months slide in, the chosen day glides to its new place, and ranges fill as a soft band.

items.name: DatePicker
items.description: A date field you can type into, with a calendar in a popover. On phones the calendar opens as a bottom sheet.

items.name: DateRangePicker
items.description: Pick a start and end date. Wide screens show two months side by side, narrow screens one, and phones get a bottom sheet.

items.name: TimePicker
items.description: A time field that opens scroll-snap wheels for hours and minutes, in 12 or 24 hour time, with any minute step.

items.name: WeekSchedule
items.description: A week with days as columns and hours as rows. Overlapping events sit side by side, and a busy day widens so every title has room. Kinds tell events apart by fill, and a blue line marks now. On a phone it shows one day at a time, with a day strip.

items.name: Alert
items.description: Inline messages and page banners. Dismissing fades them, then folds the height so content slides up.
a11y: Warning and error use role="alert"; info and success use role="status".
Success, warning and error get a status tint and a coloured icon. The icon shape and the title still tell them apart, so colour is never alone.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant? | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error'` | `'info'` | Sets the colour and icon. Error and warning are announced at once. |
| title? | `ReactNode` |  | Short bold line at the top. |
| children? | `ReactNode` |  | Body text under the title. |
| onDismiss? | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button. Called after the collapse animation. |
| dismissLabel? | `string` | `'Dismiss'` | Screen reader name for the close button. |
| banner? | `boolean` |  | Full-width strip for the top of a page. |
| action? | `ReactNode` |  | Button or link shown under the text. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<Alert variant="info" title="New version available">Reload to update.</Alert>
<Alert variant="error" title="Payment failed" onDismiss={hide}>Your card was declined.</Alert>

items.name: EmptyState
items.description: What to show when there is nothing yet. Icon, title, text and action rise in order.
a11y: One primary action. The heading level is set by headingLevel.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | Short heading that says what is empty. |
| description? | `ReactNode` |  | Text under the title, such as what to do next. |
| icon? | `ReactNode` | `<InboxIcon />` | Picture above the title. It is hidden from screen readers. |
| action? | `ReactNode` |  | One primary action, plus an optional secondary one. |
| secondaryAction? | `ReactNode` |  | Less important action, shown before the primary one. |
| headingLevel? | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `3` | Heading level for the title, to fit the page outline. Use 1 when the empty state is the whole page. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<EmptyState
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Projects keep your files in one place."
  action={<Button leadingIcon={<PlusIcon />}>New project</Button>}
/>

items.name: ProgressBar
items.description: Determinate bars glide to their value; indeterminate bars sweep while the length is unknown.
a11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow when known, none when not.
hideLabel keeps the name for screen readers.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Says what is in progress. Shown above the bar and read by screen readers. |
| value? | `number` |  | 0 to max. Leave undefined for an indeterminate bar. |
| max? | `number` | `100` | The value that means done. |
| showValue? | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the percentage next to the label. |
| hideLabel? | `boolean` |  | Hides the label visually but keeps it for screen readers. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Thickness of the bar. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<ProgressBar label="Uploading files" value={35} />
<ProgressBar label="Preparing export" />

items.name: Meter
items.description: A measurement inside a known range, such as storage used or battery left. Ranges like the HTML meter set a tone, shown with a word and an icon.
a11y: role="meter" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext.
The tone word joins the spoken value, such as "72 GB of 100 GB, Fair".
Each tone has an icon and a word as well as a colour, so it never relies on colour alone.
Use ProgressBar for a task that finishes. A meter is a reading that can go up and down.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Says what is measured. Shown above the bar and read by screen readers. |
| value | `number` |  | The measurement, from min to max. |
| min? | `number` | `0` | Lowest possible value. |
| max? | `number` | `100` | Highest possible value. |
| low? | `number` |  | Top of the low range, as in the HTML meter. Set low or high to turn the tones on. |
| high? | `number` |  | Bottom of the high range, as in the HTML meter. |
| optimum? | `number` |  | The best value. The range it falls in is good, the next is fair, the far one poor. Undefined is the middle. |
| valueText? | `string` |  | Shown and spoken instead of the percentage, such as "72 GB of 100 GB". |
| showValue? | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the value next to the label. |
| hideLabel? | `boolean` |  | Hides the label visually but keeps it for screen readers. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Thickness of the bar. |
| labels? | `Partial<MeterLabels>` |  | Words for each tone, shown with its icon and spoken with the value. Missing keys use the English defaults. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<Meter label="Storage" value={72} valueText="72 GB of 100 GB" low={70} high={90} optimum={0} />
<Meter label="Battery" value={85} low={20} high={50} optimum={100} />
<Meter label="Server load" value={94} low={60} high={85} optimum={0} />

items.name: Route
items.description: Progress as a journey: stops along a road, the road behind drawn in ink and the road ahead dashed, with a marker that travels between the stops. For deliveries, bookings and anything that moves through set stages.

items.name: Skeleton
items.description: Grey shapes with a soft shimmer that stand in for content while it loads, or a sketch of dashed outlines for a quieter wait.
a11y: Hidden from screen readers. Give the container role="status", aria-busy and a label, so the label is read.
Shimmer stops with reduced motion.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shape? | `'text' \| 'rect' \| 'circle'` | `'rect'` | Text draws lines, rect a box, circle a round shape such as an avatar. |
| width? | `CSSProperties['width']` |  | Any CSS width, such as 120 or "50%". |
| height? | `CSSProperties['height']` |  | Any CSS height. Ignored for text, where lines set the height. |
| lines? | `number` | `1` | For text: number of lines. The last one is shorter, like real text. |
| variant? | `'solid' \| 'sketch'` | `'solid'` | Solid grey shapes, or a sketch: the same shapes as dashed outlines, like a pencil layout. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.name: Spinner
items.description: A breathing arc for short waits. It has role="status" and a spoken label.
a11y: role="status" with "Loading" (or your label).
Pass label={null} when a parent already announces the wait.
With reduced motion it turns slowly instead of stopping, so it still reads as busy.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Diameter of the spinner. |
| label? | `string \| null` | `'Loading'` | Spoken to screen readers. Pass null when a parent already announces the busy state. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<Spinner size="sm" />
<Spinner size="lg" label="Loading files" />

items.name: ProgressRing
items.description: Circular progress. The arc grows with each step; at 100% the number gives way to a drawn tick. Leave out value for an indeterminate ring.

items.name: PullToRefresh
items.description: Pull a list down from the top to load what is new. A ring draws itself in as you pull and closes past the line; past it the list stretches. Let go and it glides onto the spinner.

items.name: LivePill
items.description: A small status pill for something live, such as a download, a delivery or a timer. Tap it and its surface grows into a card from its own spot, with the pill's words still on the same pixels as the card's last row. It can be its own progress bar, and news can open it by itself.
a11y: The pill is a real button with aria-expanded, named by label with the whole state in words, such as "Map download, 63%".
Escape or a tap outside folds it back. If focus was in the card, it goes back to the pill.
While it is small, the card's content is inert and hidden from screen readers.
One polite status says news and alerts once each. A ticking number is never read out.
An alert opens it and it shrinks back after alertMs (5 seconds). A hand or focus on it holds it open.
At the bottom it sits in thumb reach; fixed, it keeps 16px plus the safe area from the screen edge.
With reduced motion it opens and closes at once.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Screen reader name of the pill, the whole state in words, such as "Map download, 63%". |
| compact | `ReactNode` |  | What the small pill shows, such as an icon, a word and a number. It stays on its spot when the pill opens. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | What the open card shows above (or below) the pill's own row. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Whether it is open, when you control it. |
| defaultOpen? | `boolean` | `false` | Starting open state when you do not control it. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new open state. |
| placement? | `'bottom' \| 'top'` | `'bottom'` | Where it sits. At the bottom it is in thumb reach and grows up; at the top it grows down. |
| fixed? | `boolean` | `false` | Pins it to the screen edge, clear of the safe area. Leave off to place it yourself. |
| progress? | `number` |  | From 0 to 1: the pill fills from its start like a progress bar, and its words change ink under the fill. |
| tone? | `'paper' \| 'ink'` | `'paper'` | "paper" is a light pill with an outline; "ink" is a solid dark one. |
| news? | `string` |  | News for screen readers, said once each time it changes, such as "Download paused". Never a ticking number. |
| alert? | `string` |  | News that opens the pill by itself, such as "Rider is at your door". Said once, and the pill shrinks back after alertMs. |
| alertMs? | `number` | `5000` | How long an alert keeps it open, in ms. A hand or focus on the pill holds it open. |

items.example:
City map {pct} } >

Offline map: city centre and the old town

items.name: Input
items.description: A text field with a top or floating label. On focus a dark edge flows both ways round it from where you click and meets on the far side. Help and error text slide in below it.
a11y: label is required. A placeholder is only an example.
Help and error are linked with aria-describedby; the error sets aria-invalid.
The error has an icon and heavier border, so it does not rely on colour.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Always required. A placeholder is only an example, never the label. |
| labelPlacement? | `'top' \| 'floating'` | `'top'` | "top" puts the label above the field, "floating" puts it inside and moves it up. |
| help? | `ReactNode` |  | Hint under the field. Hidden while there is an error. |
| error? | `ReactNode` |  | Error message under the field. Marks the field invalid. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Height of the field. sm (32px) suits toolbars and dense side panels; on touch screens it keeps 16px text so phones do not zoom. |
| leading? | `ReactNode` |  | Icon or text inside the field, before the input. |
| trailing? | `ReactNode` |  | Icon, text or buttons inside the field, after the input. |
| optional? | `boolean` |  | Adds "(optional)" after the label. |
| labels? | `Partial<InputLabels>` |  | Text added to the label, so you can translate it. Missing keys use the English defaults. |

items.example:
<Input
  label="Email"
  type="email"
  placeholder="name@example.com"
  value={email}
  onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
  help="We only use it to send your receipt."
  error={!valid ? 'Enter an email like name@example.com.' : undefined}
/>

items.name: InputGroup
items.description: A field with text, an icon or a button joined to either side, inside one border and one focus ring.
a11y: The field keeps its own visible label. A placeholder is only an example.
Text on either side, such as a unit, joins the field's description, so it is read with the field.
A button on either side is a real button with its own name and its own focus ring.
A press on a shaded side cell puts the caret in the field.
The error sets aria-invalid, shows an icon and thickens the border, so it does not rely on colour.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Always required. A placeholder is only an example, never the label. |
| hideLabel? | `boolean` |  | Hides the label visually but keeps it as the field's name, for a field whose purpose is plain from what is around it. |
| prefix? | `ReactNode` |  | Joined before the field: text or an icon in a shaded cell, or a Button, IconButton or CopyButton. |
| suffix? | `ReactNode` |  | Joined after the field, the same way as prefix. |
| help? | `ReactNode` |  | Hint under the field. Hidden while there is an error. |
| error? | `ReactNode` |  | Error message under the field. Marks the group invalid. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Height of the group, matching Input. |

items.example:
<InputGroup
  label="Price per seat"
  prefix="RM"
  suffix="a month"
  inputMode="decimal"
  value={price}
  onChange={(e) => setPrice(e.target.value)}
  help="Before tax."
  error={bad ? 'Enter a price like 49 or 49.90.' : undefined}
/>

items.name: Textarea
items.description: A multi-line field that grows smoothly with its text, up to maxRows, with an optional live count. On focus a dark edge flows round it from where you click.
a11y: Visible label and aria-describedby for help, error and count.
Native maxLength, so the limit is enforced for everyone.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Visible name of the field, also read by screen readers. |
| help? | `ReactNode` |  | Hint under the field. Hidden while an error shows. |
| error? | `ReactNode` |  | Error message under the field. Also marks the field invalid. |
| autoGrow? | `boolean` | `true` | Grows with the text. Default true. |
| minRows? | `number` | `3` | Height in lines when empty. |
| maxRows? | `number` | `10` | Most lines it grows to before it scrolls. Only used with autoGrow. |
| showCount? | `boolean` |  | Shows a live "n / max" count when maxLength is set. |

items.example:
<Textarea label="Message" maxLength={280} showCount minRows={2} maxRows={8} />
<Textarea label="Bio" error="Keep it under 3 lines." />

items.name: Select
items.description: A custom listbox. The list grows out of the field, a dark edge flows round the field, options stagger in, and one highlight glides between them.
a11y: WAI-ARIA select-only combobox: focus stays on the button, aria-activedescendant tracks the option.
Up, Down, Home, End, Enter, Space, Esc, Tab and type-ahead all work.
Disabled options are skipped by the keyboard.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Visible name of the field, also read by screen readers. |
| hideLabel? | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the label for screen readers only, for a list where a column heading already names the field. |
| options | `SelectOption[]` |  | Choices in the list, in order. |
| value? | `string \| null` |  | Selected value, when you control it. Null means nothing is chosen. |
| defaultValue? | `string \| null` | `null` | Starting value when you do not control it. |
| onValueChange? | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called when the selected value changes, with the new value. |
| placeholder? | `string` | `'Choose one'` | Shown when nothing is chosen yet. |
| help? | `ReactNode` |  | Hint under the field. Hidden while an error shows. |
| error? | `ReactNode` |  | Error message under the field. Also marks the field invalid. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  | Stops the list from opening. |
| name? | `string` |  | Submits the selected value in a hidden field with this name. |
| id? | `string` |  | Id of the button, so a `<label htmlFor>` can point at it. Inner ids add a suffix to it. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
const projects = [
  { value: 'launch', label: 'Version 3.0 launch' },
  { value: 'billing', label: 'Billing', hint: 'Archived, ask an admin' },
  { value: 'audit', label: 'Audit log', disabled: true },
]

<Select label="Project" options={projects} defaultValue="launch" />
<Select label="Report day" placeholder="Pick a day" options={days} error="Choose a day." />

items.name: Checkbox
items.description: A native checkbox that fills like a cup from the side you tap, then draws its tick. Clearing it drains it. Supports the mixed state.
a11y: Native input, so Space toggles and forms submit it.
indeterminate sets the real DOM property, read as "mixed".
The whole 44px row is clickable through the label.
error sets aria-invalid and joins the message to aria-describedby, after the description.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | Visible text next to the box. Clicking it toggles the box. |
| description? | `ReactNode` |  | Muted text under the label, linked with aria-describedby. |
| checked? | `boolean` |  | Checked state, when you control it. |
| defaultChecked? | `boolean` | `false` | Starting checked state when you do not control it. |
| onCheckedChange? | `(checked: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the checked state changes, with the new state. |
| indeterminate? | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a dash. A click clears the dash and checks the box. |
| error? | `ReactNode` |  | Error message under the label. Marks the box invalid. |

items.example:
<Checkbox label="Remember me" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Email me product news" description="About once a month." />

items.name: CheckboxGroup
items.description: Checkboxes in a fieldset that share one list of values, with a legend, a description and one error for the group.
a11y: fieldset and legend name the group; the description and the error are linked to it with aria-describedby.
Each box is a native checkbox, so Tab reaches each one and Space ticks it.
An error marks every box invalid, gives the empty ones a red edge and shows an icon, so it does not rely on colour.

items.name: Dial
items.description: Turn a round dial to set a value. It follows the hand, and a let-go glides onto the nearest step. Strong marks stand out on the scale. Three looks share one API: a knob with its scale printed on it, a solid knob with a few named levels, and the rim of a large dial you swipe sideways.
a11y: A slider in the tab order, named by its visible label. Its value text comes from formatValue; the mercury look adds the level's place, such as "Medium, 3 of 5".
Up and Right add one step, Down and Left take one away. Page Up and Page Down jump to the next labelled mark. Home and End go to the ends.
The pull only shapes a drag. Keys move one step at a time, and screen readers hear the value it lands on.
The mouse wheel never turns it, except the arc look by a sideways swipe or Shift and the wheel, so the page always scrolls.
The printed and mercury knobs take the whole touch for turning; the arc takes only sideways moves, so the page still scrolls under a finger on it.
With reduced motion it lands on the value at once, with no glide.

items.name: RulerScrubber
items.description: Drag a ruler under a fixed needle to set a number, or flick it and it coasts. It follows the hand, and a let-go glides onto the nearest tick. Strong marks stand out. While it moves, the ticks near the needle lean toward it like iron filings; at rest the ruler lies flat.
a11y: A slider in the tab order, named by its visible label, with its value text from formatValue.
Up and Right add one step, Down and Left take one away. Page Up and Page Down jump to the next numbered tick. Home and End go to the ends.
Hold Shift while dragging for steps four times finer.
Only sideways moves drag it, so the page still scrolls under a finger on it. A plain mouse wheel scrolls the page; a sideways swipe or Shift and the wheel moves the ruler.
With reduced motion it lands at once, the ticks never lean, and the drag still pulls onto each tick.

items.name: PickerWheel
items.description: A 3D wheel for any list, in one column or several, as phones pick a time. It follows the hand, and a let-go glides onto a row. Strong rows stand out, and Page Up and Page Down jump to them. TimeWheel and DateWheel set it up for a time, and for a date with each month's real length.

Typing jumps to the row that starts with what you type, such as a month name or a year.
The mouse wheel turns a column only once it has focus, and at an end the page scrolls on.
A tap on a row goes to it. Swiping on the wheel turns it, so leave room beside it to scroll the page.
With reduced motion a column lands at once, with no coast.

| disabled? | `boolean` |  | Turns off every field inside, natively, so none of them can be focused or sent. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The fields. |

items.name: ToggleGroup

items.name: RichTextEditor

items.name: IcInput
items.description: A field for a Malaysian MyKad number. It adds the dashes as you type and checks the date and place of birth.

items.name: PhoneInput
items.description: A Malaysian phone number field with a fixed +60. It formats mobiles and landlines as you type and gives you E.164.

items.name: CurrencyInput

items.name: AddressFields

items.name: InlineEdit

items.name: MentionInput
items.description: A text box where typing @ opens a list of people. The value is plain text plus the ids of everyone mentioned.

items.name: ColorPicker
items.description: Pick a colour on a saturation and brightness area with a hue slider, type a hex code, or tap a preset. The value is always a six digit hex code.

items.name: SignaturePad
items.description: Sign with a finger, pen or mouse. Lines are smoothed, a pen’s pressure sets their weight, and Undo steps back one line or brings back a cleared pad.

items.name: EmojiPicker
items.description: About 400 common emoji in groups, with search by name, arrow keys and a recently used row.

items.name: Prose
items.description: Long text written elsewhere, such as Markdown or a CMS, set for reading: headings, lists, quotes, code and pictures, on a line about 68 characters long. It styles the plain HTML inside it, so nothing needs a class.
a11y: It only styles; the HTML keeps its own meaning, so use real headings in order, lists and blockquotes.
Links are underlined, so they read as links without colour.
Every rule has zero weight (:where), so a class you add inside always wins.
Wide tables and code scroll sideways inside their own box instead of widening the page.

props.table:

items.name: Carousel
items.description: Slides on native scroll snap: swipe, trackpad, arrows, dots and keys. Autoplay is optional and shows the time left in the current dot.

items.name: ScrollArea
items.description: Native scrolling with a thin drawn scrollbar that fades in while you scroll and widens when you reach for it.
a11y: The viewport is a labelled region and takes focus, so arrow keys and Page keys scroll it.
Wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling are the browser’s own.
The drawn bar is hidden from screen readers; it is a mouse convenience.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | `string` |  | Name of the scrollable region. Required, because the region takes keyboard focus. |
| maxHeight? | `CSSProperties['maxHeight']` |  | Any CSS length, such as 320 or "50vh". |
| orientation? | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'` | `'vertical'` | Which ways the content can scroll, and which scrollbars show. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content that scrolls. |

items.example: <ScrollArea label="Release notes" maxHeight={220}>…</ScrollArea>

items.name: Collapsible
items.description: One section that shows and hides with a smooth height change. Bring your own trigger or use the built-in one.
a11y: The trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Hidden content is inert, so Tab skips it.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label? | `ReactNode` |  | Text for the built-in toggle button. |
| trigger? | `ReactElement<TriggerProps>` |  | Your own button instead of the built-in one. It gets aria-expanded and aria-controls. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Open state, when you control it. |
| defaultOpen? | `boolean` | `false` | Starting open state when you do not control it. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the open state changes, with the new state. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  | Stops the panel from opening or closing. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content shown when open. |

items.example: <Collapsible label="Show advanced options">…</Collapsible>

items.name: Stack
items.description: Puts items in a column with the same space between each one.
a11y: Adds no role. Use as="ul", "section", "nav" or "form" to give the group real meaning.
As a list it drops the bullets. Safari then stops reading it as a list, so add role="list" when the count matters.
Visual order is the DOM order, so reading and Tab order match.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap? | `Space` | `5` | Space between items, as a step of the space scale (0 to 12, read as --hl-space-N). |
| align? | `'stretch' \| 'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` | `'stretch'` | Lines items up across the stack. "stretch" makes each item full width. |
| as? | `'div' \| 'section' \| 'article' \| 'aside' \| 'nav' \| 'header' \| 'footer' \| 'main' \| 'form' \| 'fieldset' \| 'ul' \| 'ol'` | `'div'` | Element to render, so the stack can be a list, a section or a form. |

items.example:
<Stack gap={2}>…</Stack>
<Stack gap={5}>…</Stack>
<Stack gap={8}>…</Stack>

items.name: Cluster
items.description: Puts items in a row that wraps onto the next line when it runs out of room. For buttons, tags and toolbars.
a11y: Adds no role. Use as="ul" or as="nav" when the items form a list or a menu of links.
justify only moves items on screen. The DOM order stays the reading and Tab order.
wrap={false} can push items out of view. Let the row scroll, so every item stays reachable.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gap? | `Space` | `3` | Space between items, as a step of the space scale (0 to 12, read as --hl-space-N). |
| rowGap? | `Space` |  | Space between wrapped rows. Defaults to the same step as gap. |
| align? | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'baseline' \| 'stretch'` | `'center'` | Lines items up inside a row. "baseline" keeps mixed text sizes on one line. |
| justify? | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end' \| 'between'` | `'start'` | Places items along the row. "between" pushes the first and last item to the edges. |
| wrap? | `boolean` | `true` | Lets items flow onto the next row when they run out of room. |
| as? | `'div' \| 'section' \| 'nav' \| 'header' \| 'footer' \| 'ul' \| 'ol'` | `'div'` | Element to render, so a row of links can be a nav or a list. |

items.name: Grid
items.description: Lays items out in columns. Give a fixed count, or a smallest cell width and the grid drops columns as it narrows, down to one on a phone.
a11y: Adds no role. Use as="ul" for a set of cards or photos.
Items fill row by row in DOM order, so reading order matches what you see.
No media queries: the columns follow the space the grid really has.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| columns? | `number` |  | Fixed number of columns. With min, it becomes the most columns the grid may show. |
| min? | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| (string & {})` |  | Narrowest a cell may get before a column drops: a token size or any CSS length. Defaults to "md" when columns is not set. |
| gap? | `Space` | `5` | Space between cells, as a step of the space scale (0 to 12, read as --hl-space-N). |
| as? | `'div' \| 'section' \| 'ul' \| 'ol'` | `'div'` | Element to render, so a set of cards can be a list. |
| steps? | `'all' \| 'halves'` | `'all'` | With columns and min: "halves" steps from columns to half of it, then to one (4, 2, 1), so no card is left alone on a row. |

items.example:
<Grid min="md" gap={5}>
  {projects.map((p) => <Card key={p.id} title={p.title} … />)}
</Grid>

items.name: Container
items.description: Holds page content at a readable width, centred, with side padding that clears the notch on a phone.
a11y: Adds no role. Use as="main" for the page body, so there is a main landmark.
A narrow size keeps lines short enough to read with ease.
Side padding is never less than the safe area, so content stays clear of the notch in landscape.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| 'full'` | `'lg'` | Widest the content gets, from the --hl-container-* tokens. "full" never stops growing. |
| padding? | `Space` | `5` | Space on the left and right, as a step of the space scale. The notch area on a phone wins when it is wider. |
| as? | `'div' \| 'main' \| 'section' \| 'article' \| 'header' \| 'footer'` | `'div'` | Element to render, such as main for the page body. |

items.example:
<Container as="main" size="md">
  …page content
</Container>

items.name: Split
items.description: A sidebar next to the main content. When its own box gets narrow, the two stack into one column.
a11y: Adds no role. Wrap the sidebar in aside, nav or fieldset as fits its content.
The sidebar comes first in the DOM with side="start" and last with side="end", so it reads in the order you see.
It follows the width of its own box (container query), so it also works inside panels and dialogs.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sidebar | `ReactNode` |  | Content of the narrow column, such as filters or a table of contents. |
| side? | `'start' \| 'end'` | `'start'` | Which side the sidebar sits on. It also comes first ("start") or last ("end") when the columns stack. |
| sidebarWidth? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Width of the sidebar, from the --hl-split-side-* tokens. |
| gap? | `Space` | `7` | Space between the columns, and between them once stacked, as a step of the space scale. |
| stacked? | `'both' \| 'main' \| 'sidebar'` | `'both'` | What shows once the columns stack: both, only main, or only the sidebar. |

items.example:
<Split sidebar={<Filters />}>
  <Grid min="sm" gap={4}>…cards</Grid>
</Split>

items.name: Center
items.description: Centres its content across, or across and down. Good for empty states and error pages.
a11y: Adds no role. Use as="main" for a full page error, so it has a main landmark.
Items stay in DOM order, so the heading still comes before the action.
centerText is on by default. Turn it off for more than two lines, which read better from the left.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| axis? | `'both' \| 'inline'` | `'both'` | "both" centres across and down; "inline" only across, and content starts at the top. |
| minHeight? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'screen'` |  | Least height of the box, from the --hl-center-h-* tokens. "screen" fills the visible screen. Down centring needs a height to work in. |
| centerText? | `boolean` | `true` | Centres each line of text too. Turn off for long text that reads better from the left. |
| gap? | `Space` | `4` | Space between the items, as a step of the space scale. |
| as? | `'div' \| 'section' \| 'main' \| 'article'` | `'div'` | Element to render, such as main for a full page error. |

items.name: AspectRatio
items.description: Keeps a box at a set shape, such as 16 by 9. The child fills it, and images and videos crop to fit.
a11y: Adds no role. The image inside still needs its own alt text, or alt="" when it is only decoration.
The space is held before the image loads, so the page does not jump under the reader.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ratio? | `number` | `16 / 9` | Width over height, such as 16 / 9 or 1 for a square. |

items.name: VisuallyHidden
items.description: Text that screen readers say but the screen does not show. The focusable kind shows while it has focus, for skip links.
a11y: Uses the clip pattern, not display: none, so the text stays in the accessibility tree.
Good for making repeated links unique, such as "Read more about Mobile app".
The focusable kind shows on keyboard focus, so a sighted keyboard user never tabs onto something they cannot see.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| focusable? | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the content while something inside it has keyboard focus, such as a skip link. |

items.example:
<Link href={url}>
  Read more<VisuallyHidden> about {project.title}</VisuallyHidden>
</Link>

items.name: ResizablePanels
items.description: Two or more panels with handles you drag or move with the keys. Min and max sizes, collapse, side by side or stacked, and snap places a handle lands on when let go near one.

items.name: MasonryGrid
items.description: Cells of mixed heights packed into columns with no gaps between rows. The column count follows the width, and the order stays left to right, row by row.

items.name: GlassLens
items.description: For the Glass theme: a clear rim round the Navbar pill that bends the page under it, like the edge of a lens. Render it once. Chromium browsers get the bend; others keep the frosted glass.

items.name: Image
items.description: An image that keeps its space, loads from a blurred placeholder into focus, and shows a calm fallback when it fails.

items.name: Lightbox
items.description: Open a photo large. It zooms out of its thumbnail, swipes or arrows to the next one, and shrinks back on close. A flick is enough to change photo or close, and a short drag glides back.

items.name: HoverCard
items.description: A preview card that opens after a short pause on hover or keyboard focus. On touch, the first tap opens it and a second tap follows the link.

items.name: Marquee
items.description: An endless row that scrolls on its own. It holds still while hovered, focused or pressed and held, and stops under reduced motion.

items.name: VideoPlayer
items.description: Quiet controls over a native video: seek, volume, captions, speed, full screen and picture in picture. The controls fade while it plays.

items.name: AudioPlayer
items.description: A compact player for voice notes and recordings: play, seek, time, speed and an optional waveform drawn from peaks you pass.

items.name: QrCode
items.description: A QR code drawn as crisp SVG from any text, with its own encoder: versions 1 to 40, all four error correction levels and automatic mask choice.

items.name: ImageCropper
items.description: Crop and zoom one photo inside a fixed frame. Drag to move it, pinch or scroll to zoom. It gives back the crop in pixels of the original photo, ready for a canvas.

items.name: CompareSlider
items.description: Two versions of one picture, one over the other, split by a divider you drag. Click or drag anywhere on the picture to move it.

items.name: Retime
items.description: Lets people choose how fast motion plays: off, slower, normal or faster. One choice retimes every component, and it is remembered on the device.
a11y: A labelled SegmentedControl: arrow keys move between speeds.
Goes further than reduced motion, which is all or nothing: some people want motion slower, not gone.
Reduced motion in the system still wins, whatever is picked here.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label? | `string` | `'Motion'` | Visible label. |
| value? | `'off' \| 'slower' \| 'normal' \| 'faster'` |  | The chosen speed, when you control it. |
| defaultValue? | `'off' \| 'slower' \| 'normal' \| 'faster'` | `'normal'` | Starting speed when you do not control it. A speed saved on this device wins over it. |
| onValueChange? | `(speed: RetimeSpeed) => void` |  | Called with the new speed. |
| remember? | `boolean` | `true` | Saves the choice on this device, so it lasts across visits. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md'` | `'md'` | Height of the control. |
| labels? | `Partial<RetimeLabels>` |  | Text for each speed, so you can translate it. |
| fullWidth? | `boolean` |  | Fills the row, with the speeds sharing it evenly, as in a settings panel. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.name: OnionSkin
items.description: Shows what just changed: the old value stays as a faint grey ghost under the new one for a moment, like an animator’s onion skin.

items.name: Register
items.description: Keeps one thing in place across a change: give two elements the same mark and the first morphs into the second, like registration marks on a peg bar.

items.name: ScrollDraft
items.description: Draws a line drawing as it scrolls into view, like a pen following the page. It sets --draft from 0 to 1, and every SVG shape inside with pathLength="1" draws with it.

items.name: TextRise
items.description: Sets a line word by word: each word rises from behind its own baseline, a little after the one before. Or, with effect ink, a paragraph turns from grey to full ink word by word as you read down it. It follows the scroll, or plays once when it mounts.

items.name: ScrollStory
items.description: Steps scroll past a stage that stays in view. One frame travels across the stage, changing place and size for each step, and its picture changes like film through a gate. The step you are on reads in full ink.

items.name: StackScroll
items.description: Cards pile up as you scroll, like cels on a peg bar. Each one sticks a little below the last and the next slides over it. The ones underneath shrink and grey out like an onion skin, and a fast scroll tilts the moving card back until the page settles.

items.name: ScrollTrack
items.description: A row of panels pulled sideways like film through a gate. The section pins while you scroll down and the row moves across instead, with a tick for each panel. On a narrow screen it is a plain sideways swipe.

items.name: Parallax
items.description: Things at different depths move at different speeds as you scroll, like cels slid apart on a multiplane camera. A loose collage where near pictures travel further than far ones, or columns that drift apart.

items.name: ScrollTone
items.description: The paper behind a run of sections changes tone as you scroll from one to the next, like a page lit differently on each spread. It uses the theme’s own tones, so it stays in your palette, or a pair of colours you give it.

items.name: ScrollExpand
items.description: A picture or video that opens from a thin strip to the full frame as you scroll, like a gate widening in front of a lens. With through, it keeps going: it fills the whole screen and the camera pushes in, as if you go inside it, then it scrolls on like a new page.

items.name: TableOfContents
items.description: The sections of a page as links to their headings, kept beside the text. Each section is a frame on a strip: filled once read, ringed where you are, open ahead, so it shows how far through the page you are.
a11y: A nav landmark named by its title; the section being read has aria-current="location".
Real links to #ids, so each section has an address to share, and Cmd-click opens a new tab.
A click moves focus to the heading, so a screen reader carries on from there.
Scrolling is smooth only without reduced motion, and the address bar keeps one history entry.
Each link keeps a 44px hit area.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `TocItem[]` |  | The sections, in page order: each heading's id and the text to show for it. |
| title? | `string` | `'On this page'` | Heading above the list, also the nav's name. |
| backToTop? | `boolean` | `false` | Adds a way back to the top once the reader has passed the first section. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example:
<TableOfContents
  items={[
    { id: 'season', label: 'Seasoning' },
    { id: 'clean', label: 'Everyday cleaning' },
    { id: 'rust', label: 'If it rusts' },
    { id: 'store', label: 'Storing it' },
  ]}
  backToTop
/>

items.name: Tabs
items.description: Switch between views. The underline runs to the new tab, splits, and what is left drains after it; the panel rises in.
a11y: WAI-ARIA tabs with automatic activation.
Left and Right move, Home and End jump.
The list scrolls sideways on small screens instead of wrapping.

items.name: Accordion
items.description: Stacked sections that open with a smooth height change. Closed content is inert.
a11y: Header buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls; panels are labelled regions.
Up, Down, Home and End move between headers.
headingLevel keeps the page outline right.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| type? | `'single' \| 'multiple'` | `'single'` | "single" keeps one item open at a time. |
| value? | `string[]` |  | Values of the open items, when you control it. |
| defaultValue? | `string[]` | `[]` | Starting open items when you do not control it. |
| onValueChange? | `(value: string[]) => void` |  | Called when the open items change, with the new list of values. |
| headingLevel? | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `3` | Heading level for item titles, to fit the page outline. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The AccordionItem elements. |

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | `string` |  | Unique id for this item, used in the Accordion value list. |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | Text on the button that opens and closes the item. |
| disabled? | `boolean` |  | Stops the item from opening or closing. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content shown when the item is open. |

  <AccordionItem value="b" title="Can I change the accent?">…</AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

items.name: Breadcrumb
items.description: Shows where a page sits. Long paths fold into a "…" button that unfolds with a stagger.
a11y: nav landmark with an ordered list.
The last item has aria-current="page".
An item with href is a link. An item with only onClick is a real button, so Tab and Enter reach it.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `BreadcrumbItem[]` |  | Path from the top level down. The last item is the current page. |
| maxItems? | `number` | `4` | Above this many items, the middle collapses into a "…" button. With 2 or less, only "…" and the current page show. |
| label? | `string` | `'Breadcrumb'` | Name of the nav landmark. |
| expandLabel? | `string` | `'Show full path'` | Screen reader name for the "…" button. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the nav element. |

<Breadcrumb
