    { label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { label: 'Projects', href: '/projects' },
    { label: 'Version 3.0 launch', href: '/projects/launch' },
    { label: 'Files' },
  ]}
/>

items.name: Pagination
items.description: Page numbers with a pill that glides to the current page.
a11y: nav landmark; the current page has aria-current="page".
Every button is 44px. Use siblings={0} on phones so it fits 375px.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pageCount | `number` |  | Total number of pages. Pages count from 1. |
| page? | `number` |  | Current page, counting from 1, when you control it. |
| defaultPage? | `number` | `1` | Starting page when you do not control it. |
| onPageChange? | `(page: number) => void` |  | Called when the page changes, with the new page number. |
| siblings? | `number` | `1` | Pages shown on each side of the current one. |
| label? | `string` | `'Pagination'` | Screen reader name for the nav landmark. |
| previousLabel? | `string` | `'Previous page'` | Screen reader name for the previous button. |
| nextLabel? | `string` | `'Next page'` | Screen reader name for the next button. |
| pageLabel? | `(page: number) => string` | `(p) => `Page ${p}`` | Builds the screen reader name for each page button. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the root element. |

items.example: <Pagination pageCount={12} page={page} onPageChange={setPage} siblings={0} />

items.name: Stepper
items.description: Progress through a flow. Finished steps swap their number for a drawn tick and the line fills to the next.

items.name: CommandPalette
items.description: Run any command from the keyboard. Cmd K or Ctrl K opens it; fuzzy search, grouped results, recent items and a highlight that glides between rows.

items.name: Navbar
items.description: Top bar with a brand, links and actions. An underline glides to the current page. Under 640px wide it folds the links into a menu. With float, it morphs into a pill in the middle as the page scrolls, and on a phone it can pour down to dock at the bottom of the screen.

items.name: Sidebar
items.description: Side navigation in sections. A pill glides to the active item. It collapses to icons, with tooltips, and the pill follows the change in width.

items.name: BottomTabBar
items.description: Phone tabs in the thumb zone. The chosen tab takes the full ink and its icon hops once. Edge to edge or a floating dock, every label or only the chosen one, with one main action set apart or raised in the centre, and a dock that shrinks as you read.

items.name: Menubar
items.description: A desktop app menu bar, such as File, Edit and View, with submenus, checkable items, radio groups and shortcuts. In a menu, the hover fill is a bead that follows your pointer.

items.name: Toolbar
items.description: A row of buttons and toggle buttons with one tab stop. Items that do not fit move into a "More" menu.

items.name: Tooltip
items.description: A short label on hover or keyboard focus. It grows out of the side facing its trigger.
a11y: role="tooltip", linked with aria-describedby while open.
Shows on keyboard focus, hides on Esc, and stays while hovered (WCAG 1.4.13).
On touch, a tap shows it for a moment. Never put the only copy of key info in a tooltip.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| content | `ReactNode` |  | Short text shown on hover and focus. It also describes the trigger to screen readers. |
| side? | `'start' \| 'end'` | `'top'` | Preferred side of the trigger. It flips when there is no room. |
| children | `ReactElement<TriggerProps>` |  | One focusable element, such as a Button or IconButton. |
| delay? | `number` |  | Delay before showing on hover. Defaults to the tooltip delay token. |

items.example:
<Tooltip content="Tooltip on top" side="top">
  <Button variant="secondary">top</Button>
</Tooltip>

items.name: Popover
items.description: A small panel anchored to a trigger, with a title and any content. It grows out of its trigger and folds back into it.
a11y: Non-modal dialog with a heading as its name.
Focus moves in and stays while open; Esc or outside click closes and returns focus.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trigger | `ReactElement<TriggerProps>` |  | One element, such as a Button, that opens and closes the popover on click. |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | Visible heading, also the dialog's accessible name. |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content of the panel, under the title. |
| open? | `boolean` |  | Whether the panel is open, when you control it. |
| defaultOpen? | `boolean` | `false` | Starting open state when you do not control it. |
| onOpenChange? | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the panel opens or closes, with the new open state. |
| side? | `'start' \| 'end'` | `'bottom'` | Preferred side of the trigger. It flips when there is no room. |
| align? | `Align` | `'start'` | How the panel lines up with the trigger along that side. |
| closeLabel? | `string` | `'Close'` | Label for the close button. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the panel. |

items.example:
<Popover trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Set reminder</Button>} title="Remind me">
  <Select
    label="When"
    options={[
      { value: '1h', label: 'In 1 hour' },
      { value: 'morning', label: 'Tomorrow morning' },
      { value: 'week', label: 'Next week' },
    ]}
    defaultValue="1h"
  />
</Popover>

items.name: DropdownMenu
items.description: A menu of actions. It grows out of its button, items arrive in a quick stagger, and the hover fill is a bead that follows your pointer from item to item.
a11y: Menu button pattern: role="menu" and menuitem, focus moves into the menu.
Up, Down, Home, End, type-ahead, Enter, Space, Esc and Tab.
Down or Up on the trigger opens at the first or last item.
Destructive items are red and bold, never colour alone: the label says the action. Red text is at least 4.5:1 on the menu and on its highlight, in both themes.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trigger | `ReactElement<TriggerProps>` |  | One button that opens the menu. It gets the menu ARIA attributes, and an id if it has none. |
| items | `MenuEntry[]` |  | Items, separators and group labels, in menu order. |
| label? | `string` |  | Accessible name for the menu, if the trigger text is not enough. |
| align? | `Align` | `'start'` | Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. |

items.example:
<DropdownMenu
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Options</Button>}
  items={[
    { type: 'label', label: 'File' },
    { label: 'Edit', icon: <EditIcon />, shortcut: '⌘E', onSelect: edit },
    { type: 'separator' },
    { label: 'Delete', icon: <TrashIcon />, destructive: true, onSelect: remove },
  ]}
/>

items.name: Dialog
items.description: A modal that grows out of the button that opened it and folds back into it. On phones it is a bottom sheet with full-width actions: it rises from the bottom edge, or grows out of a button it covers, and you can pull it down by its handle to close it.
a11y: role="dialog" with aria-modal, title and description.
Focus is trapped and returns to the trigger; Esc closes.
dismissOnOverlay={false} for forms, so a stray tap does not lose work.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | `boolean` |  | Shows the dialog. You always control it. |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with false when the close button, Esc or an outside tap asks to close. |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | Heading of the dialog. Also its accessible name. |
| description? | `ReactNode` |  | Short text under the title, read out when the dialog opens. |
| children? | `ReactNode` |  | Main content of the dialog. |
| footer? | `ReactNode` |  | Actions row. Put the primary action last, so it sits under the thumb on phones. |
| size? | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg'` | `'md'` | Maximum width of the panel. |
| dismissOnOverlay? | `boolean` | `true` | Set false for dialogs that must not close by a stray tap, like unsaved work. |
| closeLabel? | `string` | `'Close'` | Screen reader name for the close button. |
| initialFocus? | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | Element to focus first. Defaults to the first focusable element. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the dialog panel. |

items.example:
<Dialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Delete this project?"
  description="All 24 files go away. You cannot undo this."
  footer={<>
    <Button variant="secondary" onClick={close}>Keep it</Button>
    <Button variant="danger" onClick={remove}>Delete project</Button>
  </>}
/>

items.name: AlertDialog
items.description: Asks one question before an action that cannot be taken back. Focus starts on Cancel, and a tap outside never closes it. On phones it is a bottom sheet with no handle, so only a choice closes it.
a11y: role="alertdialog" with aria-modal; the title names it and the description is read with it.
Focus starts on Cancel, the safe choice, so a stray Enter never confirms.
Esc cancels and focus returns to the button that opened it. Tab stays inside.
A tap or click outside does nothing, so the question has to be answered.
tone="danger" makes the confirm button solid red, and its label names the action, so it never relies on colour.
On phones it docks to the bottom like Dialog, with Cancel nearest the thumb.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | `boolean` |  | Shows the dialog. You always control it. |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with false after Confirm, Cancel or Esc. A tap outside never closes it. |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | The question, such as "Delete this project?". Also the accessible name. |
| description | `ReactNode` |  | What happens if they confirm. Read out with the title when the dialog opens. |
| children? | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content under the description, such as a list of what goes away. |
| confirmLabel | `string` |  | Text of the confirm button. Name the action, such as "Delete project", not "OK". |
| cancelLabel? | `string` | `'Cancel'` | Text of the cancel button. |
| onConfirm | `() => void` |  | Called when they confirm, before the dialog closes. |
| onCancel? | `() => void` |  | Called when they cancel with the button or Esc, before the dialog closes. |
| tone? | `'default' \| 'danger'` | `'default'` | "danger" gives the confirm button the solid red look, for actions that destroy something. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the dialog panel. |

items.example:
<AlertDialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  tone="danger"
  title="Delete this workspace?"
  description="Its 12 projects, files and invoices go away for everyone. You cannot undo this."
  confirmLabel="Delete workspace"
  onConfirm={remove}
/>

items.name: Sheet
items.description: A bottom sheet. It follows your finger when you drag the handle, closes on a flick or a long pull, and carries on at the speed you let go with. Pulled up, it stretches. With detents it rests at low, half or full height, a flick moves it one height, and the grabber is a real control for the height.
a11y: Same modal rules as Dialog: trap, Esc, focus return.
Drag is a shortcut only; the close button and Esc always work.
Bottom padding clears env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
With detents the grabber is a slider named by heightLabel: arrow keys, Home and End set the height, Enter or a tap steps up. It reads "Low", "Half" or "Full".
With detents it is modal only at its highest height. Lower down the page behind stays usable, with no trap and no dim. Esc steps down one height, and closes it from the lowest.
Tab onto a control hidden below the screen grows it to full height. Shrunk below the focused control, focus moves to the grabber.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | `boolean` |  | Whether the sheet is open. You always control it. |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the sheet asks to close, by Esc, outside tap, drag or close button, with false. |
| title | `ReactNode` |  | Visible heading, also the dialog's accessible name. |
| description? | `ReactNode` |  | Text under the title, also read as the dialog's description. |
| children? | `ReactNode` |  | Main content of the sheet. |
| footer? | `ReactNode` |  | Sticky actions at the bottom of the sheet. |
| closeLabel? | `string` | `'Close'` | Screen reader name for the close button. |
| initialFocus? | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | Element to focus first. Defaults to the first focusable element in the content. |
| className? | `string` |  | Extra class for the panel. |
| detents? | `SheetDetent[]` |  | Heights the sheet rests at, such as ['peek', 'half', 'full']. Below the highest one it is not modal: the page behind stays usable. |
| detent? | `'peek' \| 'half' \| 'full'` |  | The height it rests at, when you control it. |
| defaultDetent? | `'peek' \| 'half' \| 'full'` |  | The height it opens at when you do not control it. Defaults to the lowest. |
| onDetentChange? | `(detent: SheetDetent) => void` |  | Called with the new height after a drag, a tap or a key on the grabber, or Esc. |
| heightLabel? | `string` | `'Sheet height'` | Screen reader name for the grabber, which sets the height. |

items.example:
<Sheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Share project" footer={…}>
  <Input label="Email" type="email" />
</Sheet>

items.name: Toast
items.description: Short messages. A drop buds out of the screen edge under the stack, breaks free and grows into the toast; a dismiss flows back into the edge. Pass origin and, when the button that sent it is within 240px, the drop buds out of the button instead. They stack, fan out on hover, and leave on their own. Throw one sideways and it flies off at the speed of your swipe.
a11y: A polite live region reads each new toast once.
Timers pause on hover, on focus and when the tab is hidden.
Every toast has a close button; swipe is optional.

props.table:
| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Your app. Anything inside can call useToast. |
| visible? | `number` | `3` | How many toasts stay visible in the stack. |
| label? | `string` | `'Notifications'` | Name of the notification region for screen readers. |
| dismissLabel? | `string` | `'Dismiss'` | Screen reader name for each close button. The toast title is added after it. |

items.name: ContextMenu
items.description: Actions for a thing, opened where you pressed: right click, long-press on touch, or Shift F10 and the Menu key. The menu grows out of the spot you pressed; submenus grow out to the side. The hover fill is a bead that follows your pointer.

items.name: Drawer
items.description: A side panel that slides in from the left or right edge. Content follows a beat later, so the motion has depth. On a phone, swipe it back toward its edge to close it.

items.name: Tour
items.description: A guided first run: it dims the page, lights up one element at a time and explains it in a small card with Next, Back and Skip.

items.name: Forgot password
items.description: Ask for a reset link, wait for the email with a resend countdown, then choose a new password with a strength hint. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Two-step verification
items.description: Enter a 6-digit code, ask for a new one after a wait, or use a backup code. A box lets people trust their own device. In the demo, 000000 shows the error. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Onboarding
items.description: Four steps to set up a workspace: name and address, invite teammates, preferences, and a summary. Back and Next sit in a bar at the bottom, and answers are kept for the tab.

items.name: Profile
items.description: Edit a public profile: photo with a live preview, name, username, bio and up to three links, next to a preview of the public page. Save sits in a bar at the bottom. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Team members
items.description: A team page: members with their role, pending invites with resend and revoke, and an invite dialog with email and role. Removing someone or revoking an invite asks first. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Billing
items.description: Current plan, usage meters, the card on file, invoices and a change plan dialog. UI only: the card is shown masked, and "Update card" links to your payment provider. There are no card fields. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Notifications center
items.description: A full page of notifications grouped by day, with filters for unread and type, and a link to notification settings. Mark all as read sits in a bar at the bottom and can be undone. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: App shell
items.description: Desktop app layout: a sidebar in sections, a top bar with title, search and account menu, and a page of cards. Under 768px the sidebar moves into a drawer.

items.name: Phone shell
items.description: Phone-first app layout: a sticky top bar with the title, a scrolling page, and five tabs at the bottom. On a wide screen the content stays in a narrow centred column.

items.name: Sign in
items.description: Email and password sign in with remember me, a reset link and a link to sign up. A centred card on desktop; on a phone the button sits in the thumb zone. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Sign up
items.description: Name, email and password with a strength hint, and a required terms box. Same validation, loading and toast as sign in. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Dashboard
items.description: A workspace overview page: a period switch, four key numbers, two charts and the tasks that changed last. Copy the folder into your app and swap in your data.

items.name: Settings
items.description: An account settings page with profile, notifications, privacy and a danger zone. Save sits in a bar at the bottom and always says whether there is anything to save.

items.name: Status pages
items.description: Three calm full pages: nothing here yet, page not found, and something failed. Each says what happened and gives one clear next step.

items.name: Booking
items.description: A four step flow to book a demo call: date, time, details, confirm, then a success screen. Back and Continue keep everything typed so far. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Checkout
items.description: Seats and add-ons with quantity and remove, billing details and address, a setup help option, a payment method choice and an order summary in RM. Collects no card data: the real payment page comes from your payment provider.

items.name: Invoice
items.description: A printable invoice: company and client details, line items, SST and the total in RM, a status badge, and Print and Download buttons. Prints on white paper in both themes. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Help centre
items.description: Search, topic cards, popular articles, common questions and ways to reach a person. The search filters articles as you type.

items.name: Contact form
items.description: Name, email, an optional Malaysian phone number, a topic, a message with a live count and a consent box. Errors show on submit; success replaces the form.

items.name: Pricing table
items.description: Three plans with a monthly and yearly switch, RM prices, a feature comparison table and common questions. The recommended plan has a badge and a line of text, not a glow.

items.name: Event page
items.description: A community meetup with a cover photo, date, venue, host, schedule, a map block that opens Google Maps or Waze, and an RSVP form. Share copies the link; Add to calendar downloads an .ics file. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Admin console
items.description: A full workspace admin app in one shell: Members and roles, Invites, Projects (a data table), Analytics, Audit log and Purchases. A sidebar on desktop and a drawer on phones. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Marketing site
items.description: A public product website with a shared top navigation and footer: Landing, Pricing, Changelog, Help centre, Contact and Book a demo. On phones the links fold into a Menu drawer and each page's main action docks at the bottom. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: SaaS starter
items.description: The first-run journey of a SaaS app: Sign in, Sign up, Onboarding, then Dashboard, Settings and Billing inside one app shell. Copy the folder and swap in your own API.

items.name: Workspace
items.description: The daily app of a team tool: Projects, a Project board, Schedule, Inbox, Files and Search inside one app shell, with working links between them. Copy the folder and swap in your own API.

items.name: Slate
items.description: A cool grey-blue accent with softer square corners. Calm and businesslike, for tools and admin pages.

items.name: Forest
items.description: A deep green accent on the grey library. Quiet and natural, for wellness, finance or outdoor brands.

items.name: Clay
items.description: A warm terracotta accent with rounded corners in place of pills. Friendly, for shops, food and crafts.

items.name: Plum
items.description: A muted plum accent. Soft but grown-up, for studios, beauty and events.

items.name: Glass
items.description: Frosted glass for the parts that float: the Navbar pill, Dialog, Sheet, Popover, menus, Toast and the FAB actions. The page shows through, blurred. Content stays solid.

items.name: Density
items.description: Two presets that change control heights, spacing and text size together: Compact for busy tools, Comfortable for calm reading.

items.name: Inbox
items.description: A message inbox with search, an unread filter, a reading pane with replies, and archive and delete. On a phone the conversation opens as its own screen. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Project board
items.description: A Kanban board for one project, with filters by assignee and label, a card detail Drawer and an add card Dialog. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Schedule
items.description: A week calendar with a mini month, event details and an add event Dialog with DatePicker and TimePicker. On a phone it shows one day at a time. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Data table
items.description: A task table with search, filters, column sort, row selection with export, archive and delete, pages, and empty and loading states. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Analytics report
items.description: A report page with a date range, four key numbers, line, bar and donut charts, a breakdown table and a download button. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: File manager
items.description: Folders in a tree, a list or grid of files, a breadcrumb, upload, rename in place and delete. On a phone the tree hides and the breadcrumb and folder rows do the work. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Search results
items.description: A search page with results grouped by type, type and date filters, highlighted matches, and suggestions when there is nothing to show. Needs a ToastProvider above it.

items.name: Orders
items.description: An order history with status and year filters, and an order view with items, totals in RM, a progress Timeline and a help link. On a phone the order opens as its own screen.
